verses.1: And as Solomon prayed, the fire descended from heaven. It ate up the offerings and sacrifices. The glory of the LORD filled the temple.
verses.2: And the priests were not allowed to enter the House of God, because the glory of Jehovah filled the House of God.
verses.3: And all the children of Israel saw the glory of the fire, and the greatness of Jehovah upon the temple. They prostrated themselves to the ground, and they praised Jehovah, saying that it was good, for His mercy was everlasting.
verses.4: And the king and all the people offered sacrifices before Jehovah.
verses.5: And King Solomon offered sacrifices in the morning: forty and two thousand sheep, and one hundred and twenty thousand goats. He also dedicated the Temple of God, along with all the people.
verses.6: And the priests stood by their altars, and the singers sang the songs of Jehovah. These songs were created by David, the king, as an offering to Jehovah. It was as if His kindness would last forever, and His love for David continued through the hands of the priests. And all of Israel stood there, too.
verses.7: And Solomon sanctified the area in front of the Temple, as he had done with the altars and the offerings of sacrifices. This was because Solomon wanted to make sure that nothing could be used for worship there. The offerings and sacrifices couldn’t be used for any other purpose than worshiping God.
verses.8: And Solomon celebrated the festival for seven days. All of Israel, along with him, gathered together in a huge crowd. They stayed there until they reached the River Euphrates.
verses.9: And on the eighth day, they made a ceremony. For the preparation of the altar took seven days, and the festival itself also lasted seven days.
verses.10: And on the forty-third day of the seventh month, He sent the people back to their homes, filled with joy and good heart, because of the good things that Jehovah had done for David, Solomon, and Israel.
verses.11: And Solomon was able to complete the Temple of God and the King’s palace. He also succeeded in carrying out all those things that he wanted to do in the Temple of God and in his own palace.
verses.12: And God saw Shlomo in the night, and He said to him, “I have heard your prayers. I have chosen this place as my temple.”
verses.13: And the heavens will be sealed, and there will be no rain. And I will command that the land be fertile for cultivation. And if I send birds to my people…
verses.14: And my people will be obedient, those who are called by my name. They will turn away from their evil ways and come back to me. I will hear from heaven and forgive their sins. I will heal their land.
verses.15: Now, my eyes will be open, and my ears will be attentive to the prayers of this place.
verses.16: And now, I have chosen and sanctified this house, so that it may be my name forever. My eyes and heart will always be there.
verses.17: And you shall go before me, just as your father David did. You shall do all that I command you, and you shall establish my laws and judgments.
verses.18: And I have established your throne, just as I decreed for your father David. I said, “No man shall be king over Israel.”
verses.19: And if you return and abandon my laws and commandments that I have given you, and go and serve other gods instead, and worship them.
verses.20: And I will set them over my land, which I have given them. And this house, which I have consecrated to my name, I will place before me. I will give it to the rulers and leaders of all the nations.
verses.21: And this house, which was built for all generations to live in, said, “In what manner did Jehovah make this land and this house?”
verses.22: And they said, “Because they abandoned Jehovah, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of Egypt. They worshiped other gods instead, and served them. As a result, all this evil came upon them.”
